evidence: src/sqllens/_atomic.py:38-49: tempfile.mkstemp creates the file with os.open(O_EXCL, 0o600), which the stdlib documents as readable and writable only by the creating user. The file is created before any write (fdopen then write at 45-46). os.replace(tmp_path, path) at line 49 renames the inode, so the destination keeps mode 0600 on POSIX. There is no chmod in between. Subject to the process umask, which can only remove bits.

src/sqllens/_atomic.py:38-49: the only tempfile creation is tempfile.mkstemp, which opens with O_EXCL and mode 0600 on POSIX. Content is written afterward through that fd, and nothing chmods or widens the mode. The falsifying input, an existing 0644 destination replaced by --force, still gets a 0600 tempfile, because os.replace swaps the inode and the destination's mode is never copied. The umask can only remove bits from 0600, so it can't loosen it. Both atomic_write_text and atomic_write_bytes go through this one path. The docstring (lines 12-15) limits the claim to POSIX and explicitly excludes Windows ACLs.
